studio.profile.gzdoom.note.netmode: GZDoom switches to peer-to-peer with default netmode 0 in 3+ player games; a port proxy can cause drops/desync.
studio.profile.gzdoom.note.command_netmo: Add -netmode 1 to host and client commands; keep udp_peer_broadcast disabled.
studio.profile.gzdoom.note.single_client: Use one player/one ROAD client per machine. If multiple clients run on one PC, give each a separate listen port.
studio.profile.lethal.note.transport: ROAD only carries direct/LAN/local IP:port traffic; official Steam lobby/relay traffic is outside this proxy.
studio.profile.lethal.note.localhost: If the host game or mod publishes localhost:7777, the server target should stay 127.0.0.1:7777.
studio.profile.lethal.note.listen_port: Use a separate ROAD client listen port such as 25568 to avoid local UDP port conflicts with the game.
studio.profile.lethal.note.single_client: Keep udp_peer_broadcast disabled for one-player-per-machine tests.
studio.profile.lethal.launch.localhost: Client: set the game/mod localhost or LAN target to the ROAD client listen address, usually 127.0.0.1:25568.
studio.profile.bedrock.note.raknet: Bedrock uses UDP/RakNet; the server target is usually 127.0.0.1:19132.
studio.profile.bedrock.note.listen_port: Use a separate client listen port such as 19133 to reduce local port conflicts.
studio.profile.ddnet.note.direct: DDNet uses direct UDP server traffic; keep the test on direct connect instead of the Steam server browser.
studio.profile.ddnet.note.server_authori: DDNet is server-authoritative UDP; keep udp_peer_broadcast disabled.
studio.profile.ddnet.note.udp_check: Run road-proxy udp-check before the game test to establish the ROAD UDP baseline.
studio.profile.ddnet.launch.server: Server: DDNet-Server.exe with sv_port 8303 or default UDP 8303.
studio.profile.ddnet.launch.client: Client: connect to the ROAD client listen address, usually 127.0.0.1:18303.
studio.profile.java.note.tcp: Minecraft Java uses TCP; the server target is usually 127.0.0.1:25565.
studio.profile.java.note.listen_port: Use a separate client listen port such as 25568 to avoid conflicts with the local server port.
studio.note.udp_peer_broadcast_default: UDP passthrough defaults peer-broadcast to disabled. Prefer the game's own server/packet-server mode first.
studio.note.gzdoom.netmode0: GZDoom switches to peer-to-peer with default netmode 0 in 3+ player games; a port proxy can cause drops/desync.
studio.note.gzdoom.commands: For GZDoom, add -netmode 1 to host and client commands; plugin runtime.udp_peer_broadcast=false should stay disabled.
studio.note.lethal.steam_transport: Lethal Company official online mode may use Steam transport; ROAD is suitable only for direct/LAN/local IP:port traffic.
studio.note.lethal.localhost_target: If localhost publishes on %d, server plugin target should be 127.0.0.1:%d and client listen is usually 127.0.0.1:%d.
studio.note.lethal.single_client: Keep UDP peer-broadcast disabled for one-player-per-machine tests.

validate.help:
Commands:
  validate --server configs/server.json --client configs/client.json
  validate --all-configs
  validate-plugin plugins/<name>/plugin.json
  generate-config --profile gzdoom
  generate-config --profile gzdoom --client-instances 2 --client-start-port 5031
  public-server
  ping --url ws://127.0.0.1:8080/ws --count 4
  udp-check server --listen 127.0.0.1:7777
  udp-check client --target 127.0.0.1:25568 --players 3 --tickrate 30 --duration 2m
  diagnostic-bundle --out diagnostics
